target_customer: High school students and families in Chile, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia preparing for university entrance exams
problem: Quality exam preparation is expensive and in-person; students outside major cities lack affordable, personalized access.
business_model: Consumer course subscriptions and packages for entrance exam prep (video lessons, live tutoring, AI study plans)

founders.name: Joaquin Olmedo
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Institution not stated.

founders.name: Guillermo Bruchmann Tanodi
founders.background_notes: Full-stack software developer per YC page.

founders.name: Agustín Trombotto
education: Double degree: Bachelor of Applied Sciences and Computer Engineering
founders.background_notes: Began building Filadd during college, per YC page.

competitors.name: Preuniversitario UC (online)
competitors.what: Paid online prep for the Chilean university test using Zoom live classes and ebooks

competitors.name: PreUSS (Universidad San Sebastian)
competitors.what: Free online prep platform capped at 2,500 students

competitors.name: PreUnab (Universidad Andres Bello)
competitors.what: Free self-paced online prep with unlimited places

competitors.name: Mineduc alliance with Cpech, Puntaje Nacional and Pedro de Valdivia
competitors.what: Free materials such as practice tests and audiovisual resources
competitors.funding_then: Private prep firms partnering with the ministry

technical_complexity.rationale: Video courses, live tutoring tooling and study plans are standard web engineering; AI study plans came later.

defensibility.rationale: Content is replicable and many free university options existed, so defensibility came from brand, results data and distribution rather than technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent prep schools and free university platforms continued, but a 2025 ranking in Chilean press placed Filadd first among online preuniversitarios (promotional coverage).

market_need_then: COVID-19 pushed Chilean prep online in 2020 and many universities launched free online courses, showing demand and substitutes. Paid demand was unproven at founding.

identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational tagline: Get into the university of your dreams

branding.community_and_virality: Marketed in Chile as Preu Filadd; Chilean press ranked it first among online preuniversitarios in October 2025 (promotional and self-reported figures).

brand_strength.rationale: Regional recognition in Chile but little independent press about the brand; origin of the name is unknown.

outcome_analysis: Filadd grew from a Cordoba, Argentina startup into an online exam prep provider claiming over 25,000 to 30,000 students across several Latin American countries with 90 percent year over year growth. Funding found is limited to small aggregator-reported amounts, suggesting capital efficient growth, and all figures are self-reported. It remains active and recently invested in an Indian edtech startup per a regional report.
notes: Funding seen only in aggregators and one YC-profile site, so unverified and not recorded as rounds: Seedtable 125K seed in August 2021 led by Y Combinator, CB Insights 240K over 4 rounds with latest March 2022, Yespress lists regional investors (Alaya Capital and others). Founding year conflicts (2018 on YC page, 2016 per CB Insights). Search for acquisitions returned unrelated companies, so no exit found. The La Voz article could not be fetched. Founder prior employers were not found. Completeness pass: two rounds recorded from single databases (Seedtable seed August 2021 $125K; CB Insights incubator or accelerator round March 2022, amount not given). CB Insights totals about $240K over 4 rounds, so the other rounds are missing. A January 2026 startupintros seed of $2.5M does not name Filadd and was not recorded.
